newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippine stocks soar, rest of Asia mixed.
newsitem.headline: Philippine stocks soar, rest of Asia mixed.

text.p: Asia stocks were mixed on Friday as many regional currency markets were rattled after the Philippines became the second Southeast Asian country to effectively devalue its currency in just over a week.
Philippine stocks rallied on the news, while other markets in Southeast Asia weakened.
Elsewhere, Hong Kong stocks were up sharply on a technical rebound, while those in Tokyo were little changed.
On July 2, Thailand effectively devalued the baht by 15 percent, sending jitters through other Asian centres as speculation mounted over who would be next.
The authorities in the Philippines spent several days strenuously denying they would devalue the peso and selling hundreds of millions of dollars to support it.
But on Friday the central bank announced it would widen the currency's trading band in a move it said was aimed at ridding the market of speculators.
The peso fell more than 11 percent following the news to a low of 29.45 to the dollar before the Bankers Association of the Philippines halted peso/dollar onshore trading for the day.
However, Philippine stocks soared, with the main share index rising 189.99 points, or 7.57 percent, to close at 2701.14.
President Fidel Ramos defended the move as necessary to preserve the country's economic gains and called the central bank's move a "decisive action".
"It eased the tension among investors in the equities market," said Cora Guidote, head of Philippine equities at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.

Since a weaker peso makes Philippine products more competitive abroad, export-based stocks rallied, with Solid Group Inc gaining 90 centavos, or 23.68 percent, to 4.70 pesos in late trade with 12.05 million shares traded.
Bankers criticised the Philippine central bank, saying it had lost its credibility by seeming to contradict earlier statements on its foreign exchange policy.
But businessmen welcomed the change as inevitable and said it would relieve businesses of the burden of high interest rates that were needed to bolster the currency.
As the ripple effect spread through currency markets, local stock markets fell victim to some of the jitters.
In Malaysia the key index fell below 1,000 to a new 1-1/2 year low of 988.47 points before recovering to end the morning session down 6.31 points, or 0.63 percent, at 1,002.21.
Dealers said the market was encouraged by the Malaysian central bank's repeated comments of its intention to support the ringgit.
After opening stronger Thai stocks were battered as the baht dived and investors worried about how much listed firms would incur in foreign exchange losses.

"There was deep concern about the baht volatility in the market," said one broker at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities. "The baht's further weakness would result in higher foreign exchange loss of most companies than previously expected."
The baht fell sharply to a new record low around 29.90/30.00 per dollar onshore in mid-morning trade on a spillover effect from the Philippine peso's slump.
The SET index was off 6.02 points, or 0.93 percent at 643.31.

Stocks in Singapore were off 2.73 points, or 0.14 percent, at 1,965.61 in quiet trading ahead of the release of the budget later on Friday, while Indonesian shares slumped 4.50 points, or 0.62 percent, to 724.66.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index was up 240.30 points, or 1.62 percent, at 15,079.98.
Concern over troubles in the financial sector weakened shares in Tokyo, despite buying interest in high tech issues.
The key Nikkei 225-share index was up 51.10 points, or 0.26 percent, at 19,806.98.

Buying of small-cap stocks limited the decline in South Korean stocks, leaving the index off 1.60 points at 766.17 at midday. Taiwan shares fell on profit-taking, with the index down 35.11 points, or 0.37 percent, at 9,394.63. Earlier, it had risen to 9,526.74, a seven-year intraday high.
Australia's All Ordinaries Index was up 3.1 points, or 0.12 percent, at 2,697.5, while New Zealand shares were up 9.64 points at 2,516.84.
